# Exact projective-energy blow-up at a facet

This is an ordinary dimension-reduction theorem, not a mixed depth
selector or an OC conclusion. the contributor and Defect independently derived
the compactness/Fatou proof below. The ordinary energy and affine
scaling are from
`candidate 5811f0ad1132ce56`.
The optimal denominator floor is proved in
`candidate c0fc791108fc8765`,
Section2, independently audited by Defect.

Let K be a convex body in R^(d-1) times[0,infinity), d>=1, and suppose

    F={z:(z,0) in K}

is a positive (d-1)-dimensional facet. Fix x in relint F and put
y_delta=(x,delta). For all sufficiently small delta>0 this is in int K.
For d=1 use the convention E_point=1. Then

    lim_(delta->0+) E_K(y_delta)/delta
          = C_d E_F(x),
    C_d=((d+1)/d)^(d+1).                                (1)

There is also convergence of the ACTUAL minimizing parameters. Write
the minimizing denominator for K at y_delta as

    1+c_delta.(z-x)+beta_delta(t-delta).

If a_F is the unique optimal parameter for F at x (empty in d=1), then

    c_delta -> (d/(d+1)) a_F,
    delta beta_delta -> 1/(d+1).                        (2)

No regularity of K beyond convexity and the positive facet is assumed.

## 1. Local geometry after normal dilation

For delta>0 apply the linear map(z,t)->(z,t/delta), and call the body
K_delta. Its marked point is Y=(x,1), and affine covariance gives

    E_(K_delta)(Y)=E_K(y_delta)/delta.                   (3)

Its tangential projection is contained in the fixed compact convex
projection D=proj_(R^(d-1)) K. At any fixed height s>=0 its section is
K cap {t=delta s}, viewed tangentially. These sections tend to F as
the original height tends to0, uniformly over bounded s-ranges in
the following precise sense.

The upper inclusion follows from compactness: if t_j->0 and
(z_j,t_j) in K, every convergent subsequence of z_j limits into F.
For the lower inclusion choose an interior point(q,t0) of K with
t0>0. Convexity gives

    (1-t/t0)F+(t/t0)q subset K_t,  0<=t<=t0.             (4)

Thus every compact subset of relint F is contained in all sufficiently
small positive-height sections. Together these facts show that for
every s>0, the indicator of K_delta at(z,s) tends almost everywhere
in z to the indicator of F. The only possible exceptional z are on
boundary F, which has (d-1)-volume zero. Uniformity on bounded height
ranges follows from the same compactness argument and(4).

There is a FIXED ball about Y inside every sufficiently small-delta
body K_delta. To see this choose r>0 with x+2r B_(d-1) subset F.
For 1/2<=s<=3/2, (4) contains a tangential ball centered at
(1-delta s/t0)x+(delta s/t0)q of radius(1-delta s/t0)2r.
For small delta this contains x+r B_(d-1), uniformly in s. Therefore
K_delta contains a fixed product cylinder about(x,1), and hence an
ordinary ball of some radius r0>0 about Y. This also proves the stated
interiority of y_delta. In d=1 the same assertion follows from a
positive interval[0,t0] contained in K.

## 2. The limiting prism minimization is explicit

Consider the infinite prism P=F times[0,infinity) with source Y=(x,1).
For an affine denominator

    L(z,s)=1+c.(z-x)+b(s-1)

strict positivity on P and finite integral require

    b>0,  1-b+c.(z-x)>0 on F.

In particular b<1, by testing z=x. Integration in s gives

 int_P L^(-d-1)
   =[1/(d b)] int_F[1-b+c.(z-x)]^(-d) dz
   >= E_F(x)/[d b(1-b)^d].                              (5)

For d>=2 this is exactly the(d-1)-dimensional projective energy after
putting a=c/(1-b); in d=1 the facet integral is its single value1.
The inequality is equality exactly when c=(1-b)a_F. The unique maximum
of b(1-b)^d on(0,1) occurs at b=1/(d+1). Hence the prism integral has
the unique minimizer

    b_*=1/(d+1),  c_*=d a_F/(d+1),

and its minimum is C_d E_F(x). This is a direct finite integral
calculation on an unbounded prism; it does not presume that the
compact-body minimization theorem applies to arbitrary unbounded sets.

## 3. Tightness of the ACTUAL minimizers and the lower limit

Let(c_delta,b_delta) be the minimizing parameter for K_delta at Y.
The fixed source ball from Section1 implies

    |(c_delta,b_delta)|<1/r0,                            (6)

since admissibility must hold throughout that ball. There is also a
uniform finite upper bound on the attained energies. Test c=0 and,
for example, b=1/(d+1). This denominator is positive for all s>=0,
and its inverse(d+1)-st power has a finite integral on[0,infinity).
Multiplying by the finite volume of the fixed tangential projection D
bounds every energy. For d=1 the tangential factor is1.

The audited optimal-denominator bound gives

    1+c_delta.(z-x)+b_delta(s-1)>=1/(d+1)
                                      on K_delta.       (7)

Recall why optimality is essential: the envelope derivative of
E^(1/d) is((d+1)/d)E^(1/d)a, and its concave tangent majorizes the
positive energy at every interior marked point. This forces the
optimal denominator floor on the compact body by continuity. It is
not asserted for arbitrary admissible parameters.

Take any sequence delta_j->0, and extract a convergent parameter
subsequence(c_delta,b_delta)->(c,b) using(6). Pointwise passage through
interior prism points using Section1 and(7), then continuity, gives

    1+c.(z-x)+b(s-1)>=1/(d+1) on all of P.               (8)

Thus b>=0; a negative b is impossible as s increases. If b=0 the
integrand is a positive function independent of s on a positive facet
set, and its prism integral is infinite. Local Fatou on every truncated
prism would then contradict the uniform energy upper bound. Therefore
b>0. Equation(8) at(z,s)=(x,0) also gives b<=d/(d+1)<1,
and the entire base denominator is strictly positive.

The indicator convergence of Section1 and Fatou on D times[0,infinity)
now give

 liminf_j E_(K_(delta_j))(Y)
      >=int_P[1+c.(z-x)+b(s-1)]^(-d-1)
      >=C_d E_F(x).                                    (9)

The integrands are interpreted as zero off their actual bodies. At
almost every interior prism point their denominators converge and
are positive; at other points a zero limit inferior is enough for
Fatou. This argument uses actual minimizing parameters and avoids
interchanging an infimum with a limiting integral.

## 4. Admissibility of the prism optimizer and the upper limit

Use the FIXED prism optimizer(c_*,b_*) in each large K_delta. Its base
denominator has a positive minimum m on F. At bounded heights the
upper inclusion of Section1 makes its value at least m/2 for all
sufficiently small delta. At large heights the positive term b_* s
dominates the uniformly bounded tangential term over D. More precisely,
choose S so large that for z in D and s>=S,

    1-b_*+c_*.(z-x)+b_*s>=b_*s/2.

On0<=s<=S, tangential points of K_delta are uniformly close to F,
so their denominator is at least m/2. Consequently this fixed parameter
is admissible on ALL of K_delta for small delta, and its integrand
extended by zero is bounded by

    C (1+s)^(-d-1) 1_D(z),                              (10)

for one finite constant C. The bound is integrable. Almost-everywhere
indicator convergence and dominated convergence therefore prove that
its actual K_delta integral tends to the prism minimum C_d E_F(x).
Since the actual energy is at most this test value, it follows that

    limsup_(delta->0) E_(K_delta)(Y)<=C_d E_F(x).         (11)

Combining(9),(11) proves(1). Every parameter cluster point in Section3
must attain equality in(5); uniqueness of the prism optimizer forces
(c,b)=(c_*,b_*). The bounded sequence of all actual parameters therefore
converges to this pair. Undoing the dilation gives exactly(2).

## 5. Checks, first derivatives, and scope

For an interval K=[0,H], the exact formula is

    E_K(delta)=4delta(H-delta)/H,

so the limit in(1) is4=C_1. For a d-simplex, the exact formula
E_K(y)=|K|(d+1)^(d+1) product of all barycentric coordinates
also gives(1) directly, since the vanishing apex coordinate is delta/H
and |K|=H|F|/d. These checks do not replace Sections1--4 for arbitrary
convex bodies with a facet.

The parameter convergence supplies an additional POINTWISE gradient
limit. The ordinary envelope identity grad_y E=(d+1)E a yields

    partial_delta E_K(x,delta) -> C_d E_F(x),
    grad_x E_K(x,delta)/delta -> C_d grad_x E_F(x).      (12)

For d=1 the second formula is empty. For d>=2 use
 grad_x E_F=d E_F a_F and(1),(2). No uniform C1 extension over the
boundary of the facet is asserted.

The exact lower-dimensional energy describes inward behavior along
the NORMAL above a relative interior facet point. It does not cover
lower-dimensional exposed faces, arbitrary approaches to facet edges,
or a mixed-integer depth conclusion. In particular it does not replace
a boundary zero-depth source by a proved OC center.

## 6. Exact lower-dimensional escort limit

The same proof yields a probability-level dimension recursion. On
K_delta define the normalized escort density

    rho_delta(z,s)=1_(K_delta)(z,s)
      [1+c_delta.(z-x)+b_delta(s-1)]^(-d-2)
                           /E_(K_delta)(Y).

It has mass1 and barycenter(x,1), by the ordinary escort identities.
It converges in L1 on D times[0,infinity) to

    rho_*(z,s)=1_F(z)1_{s>=0}
       [d L_F(z)/(d+1)+s/(d+1)]^(-d-2)
                                      /(C_d E_F(x)),   (13)

where L_F(z)=1+a_F.(z-x), and for d=1 use L_F=E_F=1
with counting measure on the singleton facet.

Indeed b_delta converges to the positive value1/(d+1), c_delta is
bounded, and the actual denominators have the uniform floor(7).
At large s their b_delta s terms therefore give a uniform lower bound
c(1+s); at bounded s the floor applies on their actual bodies. Their
energies converge to the positive constant C_d E_F. Thus a single
integrable multiple of(1+s)^(-d-2)1_D dominates rho_delta. The
indicator and parameter convergence from Sections1--4 prove L1
convergence by dominated convergence.

Integrating(13) in s gives the EXACT facet marginal

    integral_0^infinity rho_*(z,s)ds
                        =1_F(z)L_F(z)^(-d-1)/E_F(x).   (14)

This is precisely the lower-dimensional projective escort on F:
its exponent is(d-1)+2=d+1. The constants cancel because
(d+1)b_*=1 and[d/(d+1)]^(-d-1)=C_d.
Conditional on z, the limiting normal variable has mean

    E[s|z]=[d L_F(z)/(d+1)]/[d/(d+1)]=L_F(z).

Its total normal mean is1, since the facet escort expectation of L_F
is1. The same tail bound with the additional factor s is integrable,
so these first moments also converge. Returning to original coordinates,
the original escorts converge weakly onto the facet escort(14),
supported at height0. For a bounded continuous test function this
follows by the L1 convergence above, a uniform tail cutoff, and
uniform convergence of the argument(z,delta s) to(z,0) on that cutoff.

This is an exact ordinary escort localization onto an actual facet.
It supplies no bound for mixed cap mass and makes no claim about
lower-dimensional exposed faces that are not facets.
